info.description:
# Introduction
Welcome to CloudTalk API reference! Many of these businesses use the CloudTalk API to automate and enhance their customer support with CloudTalk Support. With CloudTalk we are re-building telco industry from the ground and taking it to the next level with first-class customer support system. Please find below the full documenation to CloudTalk.

# API Overview

The API is organized around the following resources:

API Area | Description
----------------|-------------
Calls | Browse your call history, download recordings and access all your calls data.
Contacts | Create and update Contacts. Use filters to get lists of Contacts, or access their profiles individually.
Numbers | Automate Numbers modifications. List all your numbers.
Agents | Create or update your Agents, access their settings.
Conversation Intelligence | Get Conversation Intelligence data about your calls.
VoiceAgent | Initiate VoiceAgent calls


[JSON](http://www.json.org/) is returned in all responses. XML is not supported.

The API also uses common approaches for the following:

Function | Description
----------------|-------------
Data | API data is JSON encoded with UTF-8. API JSON is either a single object or a list of objects.
Errors | 4xx and 5xx responses returning JSON with error codes
Rate Limiting | Controls how many requests can be made in a time window
HTTP | Methods are used in accordance with HTTP (GET POST and DELETE are the primary methods used) and resources are identified using URIs. All API requests are sent over HTTPS.


## Authentication

This is an HTTPS-only API. Authentication is based on API Access Key ID and Access Key Secret. The API Access Key ID and Access Key Secret is passed via HTTP Basic Authentication.

 Basic Auth credentials are used to determine on which project should this request be executed on. List of all Basic Auth credentials for the project can be found by Administrators in the CloudTalk Dashboard under Account → Settings → API Keys (https://dashboard.cloudtalk.io/menu/account/settings/API-keys).

To try the API via curl on the command-line, the general form used would be:
```
curl -u ACCESS_KEY_ID:ACCESS_KEY_SECRET API_URL
```

For instance, you would execute:
```
curl -u ABCDEFGHIJTESTKEY1:X05Dg4c331c3h61An https://my.cloudtalk.io/api/calls/index.json
```

## Usage

The API may rate limit submission of requests for your application. Such limits are managed as an allowed number of operations per time window, where an operation might be read or an update. In that case a **'429 Too Many Requests'** response code will be returned along with the following headers -

Header name | Description
----------------|-------------
X-CloudTalkAPI-Limit | Maximum number of API requests allowed in the current time window.
X-CloudTalkAPI-Remaining | Number of API requests left in the current window.
X-CloudTalkAPI-ResetTime | Time when rate limit window will be reset as a Unix timestamp.

Note that the default rate limit is **60 operations per minute per company**. If you need to make more requests, please contact our support with detailed explanation of your use case.

## Response Envelopes

**Note:** Conversation Intelligence doesn't follow envelopes.

The API returns one of three envelopes depending upon the request issued:

1. Single Item Envelope
2. Collections Envelope
3. Error Envelope

### Single Item Envelope

All dates/times are returned in ISO8601 format and in UTC timezone.

```
Status: 200 OK
{
    "responseData": {
        "id": 123,
        ...
        "created": "2018-01-10 12:34:56"
    }
}
```

### Collections Envelope

All dates/times are returned in ISO8601 format and in UTC timezone.

```
Status: 200 OK
{
    "responseData": {
        "itemsCount": 65,
        "pageCount": 3,
        "pageNumber": 1,
        "limit": 30,
        "data": [
            {
                "id": 123,
                ...
                "created": "2018-01-10 12:34:56"
            },
            {
                "id": 456,
                ...
                "created": "2017-10-19 09:21:29"
            },
            ...
        ]
    }
}
```

### Error Envelope

```
Status: 404 Not Found
{
    "responseData": {
        "status": 404,
        "message": "Not Found"
    }
}
```

## Encoding

Data is encoded as defined by JSON in [RFC4627](http://www.ietf.org/rfc/rfc4627.txt). The default encoding for APIs is UTF-8.

Some query parameters may need to be [url encoded](https://www.wikiwand.com/en/Percent-encoding) when sending - for example, the email parameter value used to query users should be encoded.

## Use of HTTP

Request methods are used in accordance with HTTP. **On the core API (`my.cloudtalk.io/api`) `PUT` creates and `POST` updates** — the reverse of the more common REST convention:

- `GET` is used to access resources and perform queries. The API does not allow modifications (creates, updates, deletes) to occur via GET.
- `PUT` is used to create resources.
- `POST` is used to update resources. PATCH is not used by the core API.
- `DELETE` is used to delete resources.

Dialer is the only surface with `PATCH` operations. Dialer and the VoiceAgent `/voice-agents` and `/knowledge-bases` operations follow the conventional mapping: `POST` creates and `PUT` replaces (on the Dialer, `PATCH` partially updates and `PUT` replaces a sub-collection wholesale). The other newer surfaces expose only a slice of the verbs — Conversation Intelligence is read-only, and CueCard is `POST`-only.

Responses use standard HTTP codes. Where there are client or server errors, a list of of one or more errors in JSON format is returned in the body.

The `Accept` header must be used by a client used to indicate a preferred response for `GET/HEAD` requests. Requests without an `Accept` header of `application/json` may be rejected with a client error of 404 or 406. The `Content-Type` header should be used by clients to indicate the submitted format for `POST/PUT` requests.

tags.description:
Partner API for the CloudTalk sales dialer — campaigns, campaign contacts, call scripts, surveys, disposition buttons, statistics and data exports.

The Dialer is a newly released product surface: depending on your account's rollout stage, campaigns managed through this API may not yet be visible in your CloudTalk Dashboard. The legacy campaigns API under `/campaigns` is a different product and is not affected.

Authentication is the same HTTP Basic scheme as the rest of the API — your API Access Key ID as the username and API Access Key Secret as the password. This surface differs from the rest of the CloudTalk API in three ways:

- **Base URL** `https://api.cloudtalk.io/v1` (not `my.cloudtalk.io/api`).
- **Responses** never use the `responseData` envelope: list endpoints return `{ data, meta }` with cursor pagination (`meta.nextCursor` — pass it back as `cursor` to page forward), single resources return the object directly, and some sub-collections return plain arrays.
- **Errors** return `{ statusCode, message, error, correlationId, subErrors? }` — except `401`, which is answered by the authentication layer in front of the host as `{ code, message }`. Quote the `correlationId` when contacting support.

Rate limiting is per company in a dedicated budget of 60 requests per minute, separate from the core API's quota.

post.description:
Emergency stop for outbound VoiceAgent dialing.

Queued calls are cancelled and calls already in progress are ended within a few seconds, through the normal call-end path — billing, call records and analytics stay correct. **Inbound calls are unaffected**, as is the outbound traffic of every other company.

The stop **expires on its own** after `duration_seconds`, so a forgotten stop cannot silence an account indefinitely. Sending the request again overwrites the window; sending `duration_seconds: 0` lifts it early.

By default the stop covers all of the company's outbound calls. Supply `voice_agent_id` to stop a single VoiceAgent while the others keep dialing.

This endpoint is rate limited to **10 requests per minute per company**, below the API-wide default of 60 — a single request already stops the whole company.

get.description:
Returns the campaign's aggregated performance on one of two bases, told apart by `range` in the response:

- **All-time** (no `dateFrom`/`dateTo`): lifetime counters served from a projection refreshed in the background — `updated_at` tells you how fresh they are, and `range` is null. `call_durations` is included only when `includeDurations=true` (it is the one read whose cost grows with the campaign).
- **Ranged** (`dateFrom` and `dateTo` both set): counters aggregated at request time over the half-open window `[dateFrom, dateTo)`. `range` echoes the resolved window, `updated_at` is null, and durations are always included (`includeDurations` is ignored).

Both bounds are RFC 3339 date-times. The service also reads the ISO 8601 date-only form `YYYY-MM-DD`, which lies outside that shape and is therefore only reachable from a client that does not validate against this schema: a date-only `dateTo` names a calendar day and is served inclusive of it — the exclusive end moves to the following UTC midnight, so equal date-only bounds are a valid one-day window. There is no limit on the window's length; the only bound is the 13-month event retention horizon on `dateFrom`. Supplying only one bound, an empty window, or a `dateFrom` past the horizon is a 422.

The membership-state blocks (`contact_states*`, `pending_by_category`, `open_assignments`) always describe the campaign's current state — a window does not narrow them. Unknown query parameters are rejected with 400 rather than ignored. A campaign that has never been dialed returns zeroed counters, not 404.

post.description:
Queues an asynchronous export of the campaign's call history or survey responses as CSV or XLSX and returns immediately with a job handle — nothing is generated during the request. Poll the job with the export-status call.

When the job completes, fetch the file through the export-download call, which mints a pre-signed link; the same link is also emailed to the requester. Optional `filters` narrow the export by contact, agent or date range — omit them to export everything for the campaign.

The call is not idempotent: every request enqueues a new job, so a retry after a timeout creates a second export and a second link. There is no deduplication window or idempotency key.

`filters.contactId` and `filters.userId` must be positive ids, and `dateFrom` / `dateTo` must be strict ISO 8601 — anything else is a 400 and no job is enqueued. Supplying only one bound is valid: a missing `dateTo` resolves to the time the job runs, a missing `dateFrom` to the campaign's creation. Each bound you do supply must itself be parseable as a date-time — strict ISO 8601 admits forms such as the week date `2026-W33` that cannot be read, and such a bound returns 422 (`dateFrom must be a parseable ISO 8601 date-time`, or the `dateTo` equivalent) whether or not the other bound is present. Supplying both with a `dateTo` that is not after `dateFrom` returns 422 (`dateTo must be after dateFrom`), and again nothing is enqueued.

post.description:
Creates an endpoint and returns it with its signing secret. This response is the only time the secret is part of the resource; read it again with `GET /webhooks/endpoints/{endpointId}/secret`.

The URL must be `https://` and point at a public host: private, loopback and other non-public addresses, internal names and non-ASCII hosts are rejected. A company can have at most 50 endpoints, Dashboard-created ones included.

Send an `Idempotency-Key` to make retries safe. A retry with the same key and the same body returns the endpoint the first request created (201), even when the company has since reached the endpoint limit. The same key with a different body is rejected with 422. After the endpoint is deleted, the key creates a new one.

name.description: Display name. Leading and trailing whitespace is trimmed before validation, so a blank or whitespace-only name is rejected with 400 (`name should not be empty` in `subErrors`).
Display name. Leading and trailing whitespace is trimmed before validation, so a blank or whitespace-only name is rejected with 400 (`name should not be empty` in `subErrors`).

questions.description: Initial question set. Omit to create an empty survey.

nextCursor.description: Opaque cursor to pass as `cursor` to fetch the next page; null when this is the last page.

DialerDispositionBreakdownEntry.description: How often one disposition tag was recorded. Labels are null when the tag cannot be resolved.

name.description: Tag display name; null when unresolvable.

color.description: Tag display colour; null when unresolvable.

outcome.description: Tag outcome classification; null when unresolvable.

DialerDispositionButton.description: One disposition button. `name`, `outcome` and `color` are resolved from the referenced call tag at read time. A button whose tag has been deleted or archived is not returned; all three are null only while the call tags cannot be read.

outcome_kind.description: How the dialer treats a call dispositioned with this button.

color.description: Colour of the referenced tag; null when the tag has no colour or the call tags cannot be read.

name.description: Display name of the referenced tag; null only while the call tags cannot be read.

outcome.description: Outcome of the referenced tag; null only while the call tags cannot be read.

DialerDispositionButtonInput.description: One disposition button in the replace-all body. The button's display name and colour are not set here — they come from the referenced tag.

tag_id.description: Referenced call-tag id. List the available tags with the disposition-tags call. Sent as an integer in requests; responses return the id as a string.

outcome_kind.description: How the dialer treats a call dispositioned with this button.

color.description: Not supported — any supplied value (including `null`) is rejected with 400. The button's colour always comes from the referenced tag. Other unknown keys are silently ignored.

DialerDispositionTag.description: One call tag usable as a campaign disposition button.

id.description: Tag ID — pass this as `tag_id` when configuring disposition buttons.

color.description: Tag display colour; null when unset.

outcome.description: Outcome classification carried by the tag.

DialerDispositionTagList.description: The company's disposition-tag catalogue. It uses the same envelope as the campaign list, but the catalogue is always returned whole, so `meta.nextCursor` is always null.

meta.description: Cursor envelope; the cursor is always null because the catalogue is unpaged.

nextCursor.description: Always null — the catalogue is returned whole.

DialerExportDownload.description: A pre-signed download link for a completed export. Minted fresh on every call; valid at least 60 minutes.

url.description: Pre-signed S3 URL of the export file. Fetch it without credentials — the signature is the authorization.

expiresAt.description: Instant the URL stops working (ISO 8601, UTC). Call the endpoint again for a fresh link.

DialerExportFilters.description: Optional narrowing filters. Omitting the whole object exports everything for the campaign. Supplying only one of `dateFrom` / `dateTo` is valid — a missing end resolves to the time the job runs, a missing start to the campaign's creation.

contactId.description: Restrict the export to one contact. Must be a positive id — `0` or a negative value is rejected with 400 (`filters.contactId must not be less than 1` in `subErrors`).

userId.description: Restrict the export to one agent (user). Must be a positive id — `0` or a negative value is rejected with 400 (`filters.userId must not be less than 1` in `subErrors`).

dateFrom.description: Only rows at or after this instant, as an RFC 3339 date-time. The service validates strict ISO 8601, so a calendar-impossible value such as `2026-02-31T00:00:00.000Z` is rejected with 400 rather than rolled forward.

dateTo.description: Only rows at or before this instant, as an RFC 3339 date-time. Validated exactly like `dateFrom`.

DialerExportJob.description: Handle for a queued export job. Poll it with the export-status call.

status.description: Job status at the moment of enqueue.

DialerExportJobStatus.description: State of an export job. Once it reports `completed`, fetch the file through the export-download call — a pre-signed link is also emailed to the requester.

createdAt.description: When the job was enqueued (ISO 8601, UTC).

completedAt.description: When the job finished; null while it is still queued or running.

DialerExportProgress.description: Coarse progress hint. Both counters stay at 0 until the runner picks the job up.

currentPartition.description: Partition the runner is currently streaming.

totalPartitions.description: Partitions the job has to stream in total.

DialerPatchCampaignRequest.description: Body of the campaign update call. Every key is optional — an omitted key is left unchanged. `status` drives the lifecycle transition; `deleted` is never a valid target here (use the delete call).

name.description: Human-readable campaign name. Leading and trailing whitespace is trimmed before validation, so a blank or whitespace-only name is rejected with 400 (`name should not be empty` in `subErrors`).

status.description: Target lifecycle status. Legal transitions: `initializing` → `active` | `archived`; `active` ↔ `inactive`; `active` → `archived`; `inactive` → `archived`; `archived` → `inactive`. A patch that leaves the status unchanged is a no-op. `deleted` passes schema validation but is always rejected with 422 — only the delete call sets it.

waterfall_order.description: Ordered, duplicate-free subset of the waterfall categories. Contacts are served tier by tier in this order.

call_script_id.description: Call script to link to the campaign; `null` clears the link, an omitted key leaves it unchanged. Sent as an integer in requests; responses return the id as a string.

survey_id.description: Survey to link to the campaign; `null` clears the link, an omitted key leaves it unchanged. Sent as an integer in requests; responses return the id as a string.

DialerPatchScriptRequest.description: Body of the patch-script call. Every field is optional; omitted fields stay untouched.

name.description: New display name. Leading and trailing whitespace is trimmed before validation, so a blank or whitespace-only name is rejected with 400 (`name should not be empty` in `subErrors`).

DialerPatchSurveyRequest.description: Body of the patch-survey call. Only these two fields are patchable — questions change through the replace-questions call.

name.description: New display name. Leading and trailing whitespace is trimmed before validation, so a blank or whitespace-only name is rejected with 400 (`name should not be empty` in `subErrors`).

is_archived.description: `true` archives the survey (its soft delete), `false` restores it.

DialerPeekContact.description: One entry of the peek answer — a non-binding snapshot of the allocator's next picks.

category.description: Waterfall category the pick came from.

phone_numbers.description: The contact's numbers in dialing order (index 0 is primary).

callback_notes.description: Note attached to a scheduled callback; null otherwise.

DialerPendingByCategoryCounts.description: Breakout of `contact_states.pending` by waterfall category — the four sum exactly to the pending total. Includes non-dialable pending contacts, so it is not an available-to-dial count.

rescheduled.description: Pending contacts whose last outcome rescheduled them.

retry.description: Pending contacts waiting on an automatic retry.

DialerQueuePolicy.description: Allocation-batch and dynamic queue-sizing bundle. Every knob is optional.

lock_size.description: How many contacts an agent may hold allocated at once.

pinned_callback_hold_ms.description: Hold window (ms) past an agent-pinned callback's due time after which any agent may serve it; 0 releases the pin as soon as the callback is overdue.

refill_amount.description: How many contacts are pulled per queue refill.

min.description: Lower bound on the dynamically sized queue.

max.description: Upper bound on the dynamically sized queue.

multiplier.description: Queue size per available agent when sizing dynamically.

threshold.description: Remaining-contact count that triggers a refill.

manual_refill.description: When true the queue is only refilled on an explicit agent action.

DialerReplaceAssociationsRequest.description: Replace-all body for a campaign's associations. Each array is optional and defaults to empty, so an omitted kind clears that kind. Every entry may be given either as an object or as a bare id. Naming the same `(kind, ref_id)` twice in one body is rejected as a conflict.

target_tag.description: Contact tags that define the campaign's membership. Naming a CRM-connection-owned tag re-ranks it in place; adding or removing such a tag is owned by the CRM connection, not this call.

queue_group.description: Queue groups the campaign draws its agents from.

DialerReplaceDispositionButtonsRequest.description: Replace-all body for a campaign's disposition buttons. A `color` key on a button is rejected with 400 — presentation always comes from the referenced tag.

buttons.description: The complete button set for the campaign. An empty array clears every button.

DialerReplaceSurveyQuestionsRequest.description: Body of the replace-questions call — the desired end state of the survey's question set. An empty array clears the survey.

DialerRetryPolicy.description: Re-dial rules bundle. Every knob is optional.

max_attempts.description: Maximum dial attempts per contact before it is exhausted.

interval_hours.description: Hours to wait between attempts; 0 retries immediately.

excluded_dispositions.description: Disposition outcomes that stop further retries.

dnc_tag_ids.description: Contact-tag ids that mark a contact as do-not-call.

DialerSchedulePolicy.description: Campaign start-window bundle. Every knob is optional.

start_date.description: Company-local calendar date the campaign may start dialing. Must be a real calendar date in `YYYY-MM-DD` — any other form, or a date that does not exist such as `2026-02-30`, is rejected with 400 (`schedule_policy.start_date must be a real calendar date in YYYY-MM-DD` in `subErrors`).

start_time.description: Company-local wall-clock time on `start_date`. Must be a valid `HH:MM` or `HH:MM:SS` time, components zero-padded and in range — any other form, or an impossible time such as `25:00`, is rejected with 400 (`schedule_policy.start_time must be a valid HH:MM or HH:MM:SS time` in `subErrors`). Omit it for midnight.

timezone_rule_enabled.description: When true the start window is applied in the contact's own timezone.

DialerScript.description: A call script agents read while dialing. Ids are BIGINTs serialized as strings.

body.description: Script content; supports `{{merge}}` fields resolved by the agent's phone at call time.

created_at.description: When the script was created (ISO 8601, UTC).

updated_at.description: When the script last changed (ISO 8601, UTC).

DialerScriptList.description: One cursor page of call scripts.

DialerStatisticsRange.description: The resolved statistics window — the field that tells you which basis the counters are on: null on an all-time response, set on a ranged one. `to` is exclusive; a date-only `dateTo` is echoed here already advanced to the following UTC midnight, so the echo may not equal the request literally.

DialerSurveyDefinition.description: A survey with its full ordered question set. Returned by every single-survey call; the list serves summaries instead.

is_archived.description: Whether the survey is archived (soft-deleted). Archiving preserves collected answers.

created_at.description: When the survey was created (ISO 8601, UTC).

updated_at.description: When the survey last changed (ISO 8601, UTC).

DialerSurveyList.description: One cursor page of survey summaries.

DialerSurveyOption.description: One choice of a `radio`, `checkbox` or `select` question. Ids are server-generated.

label.description: Choice label shown to the agent.

display_order.description: Zero-based position among the question's options.

DialerSurveyOptionInput.description: An option as sent in create/replace requests — no id.

DialerSurveyQuestion.description: One question of a survey. Ids are server-generated and change on every question replace.

label.description: Question text shown to the agent.

type.description: Input widget the agent answers with.

is_required.description: Whether the agent must answer before submitting.

display_order.description: Zero-based position among the survey's questions.

options.description: Choices for choice-type questions. Accepted and stored for any question type.

DialerSurveyQuestionInput.description: A question as sent in create/replace requests. Never carries ids — they are server-generated.

is_required.description: Whether the agent must answer. Defaults to `false`.

DialerSurveySummary.description: List item of the surveys collection — a summary carrying `question_count` instead of the questions themselves.

question_count.description: Number of questions the survey currently has.

created_at.description: When the survey was created (ISO 8601, UTC).

updated_at.description: When the survey last changed (ISO 8601, UTC).

DialerTargetTagAssociation.description: One target-tag association, with its serving rank and provenance.

priority.description: Serving rank — the highest priority is served first.

label.description: Human-readable level name; null when unset.

origin.description: Read-only provenance. `manual` rows were added through this endpoint; `crm_connection` rows are kept in sync by a campaign CRM connection and can only be re-ranked here, not added or removed.

DialerTtlPolicy.description: Contact-eligibility expiry bundle — drives how long an allocated contact stays held. Every knob is optional.

mode.description: How the expiry window is derived.

hours.description: Expiry window in hours while the campaign is running.

paused_hours.description: Expiry window in hours while the campaign is paused.

DialerError.description: Error envelope returned by every Dialer API endpoint. Note it differs from the legacy API's error format.

correlationId.description: Request correlation ID — include it when contacting support

subErrors.description: Field-level validation messages, present on validation failures

action.description: What to do when the agent cannot answer

transferConfig.description: Destination used when action is transferToHuman

defaultOutboundNumberId.description: Outbound caller id; null selects Automatic Outbound and then requires failoverOutboundNumberId

dialTimeoutSeconds.description: Ring timeout; null uses the provider default

failoverOutboundNumberId.description: Number used when Automatic Outbound cannot pick one; required with, and only allowed with, Automatic Outbound (defaultOutboundNumberId null)

goalPrompt.description: What the agent is supposed to achieve

greeting.description: Opening line; required for inbound agents

isAgentSpeakingFirst.description: Whether the agent speaks first; omitted means true for inbound and false for outbound

knowledgeBaseIds.description: Knowledge bases the agent answers from

language.description: Primary language code; rejected with 422 and the detail code LANGUAGE_NOT_SUPPORTED when no provider serves it or the agent's provider (the sent one, or the stored one on replace) does not

llm.description: Model the agent runs on, by canonical id; null on a read when the agent has none set. Omitted on create means the optimized one; omitted on replace keeps the stored value. A model the provider does not offer is rejected with 422 and the detail code LLM_OVERRIDE_NOT_AVAILABLE_FOR_PROVIDER at target llm

llmOverride.description: Deprecated alias of llm. On a read, the agent's legacy pinned model until its next save moves it into llm, else null. On a write it wins over llm when both are sent

minorVersion.description: Generation of the agent's tuned defaults. Omitted on create means the latest; omitted on replace keeps the stored value. A create takes 0 to the latest (send the source's value when duplicating an agent); a replace takes the stored value or the latest, and any other value is rejected with 422. Moving it to the latest applies the minorVersion change optimizedSettings lists

optimizedSettings.description: What applying the platform's optimized values for the agent's current setup would change. The server never applies them on its own; set each change's path to its to value and replace the agent

provider.description: Speech provider the agent runs on; null on a read when the agent has none set. Omitted on create means the optimized one; omitted on replace keeps the stored value

providerOverride.description: Deprecated alias of provider. On a read, the agent's legacy pinned provider until its next save moves it into provider, else null. On a write it wins over provider when both are sent

secondaryLanguages.description: Additional languages; the write is rejected with 422 and the detail code LANGUAGE_NOT_SUPPORTED, never trimmed, when the agent's provider does not serve a code, Deepgram included. A blank or repeated code is dropped. A Deepgram agent with secondary languages Deepgram serves is saved, and optimizedSettings then proposes ElevenLabs

status.description: Whether the agent may run; omitted on write means enabled

updatedAt.description: When the agent was last saved

verbosity.description: How much the agent elaborates; omitted means standard

isCrossfadeLoopEnabled.description: Smooth the seam when the ambience loops

volume.description: Ambience volume; null uses the provider default

calendarId.description: Calendar the appointment is created in

integrationId.description: Calendar integration the agent books in

description.description: What the agent should put in the property

interruptionIgnoreTermLanguages.description: Languages the ignored terms are given in

interruptionIgnoreTerms.description: Words that must not count as an interruption

isSpeculativeTurnEnabled.description: Let the agent prepare a reply before the caller stops speaking

isVadEnabled.description: Filter background noise with voice activity detection

turnEagerness.description: How soon the agent takes a turn

endpoint.description: HTTPS webhook the collected values are posted to

updatedAt.description: When the agent was last saved

from.description: The value the agent runs with; null when unset

path.description: Attribute path of the setting, as a write body spells it: provider, llm, minorVersion, elevenLabsSettings.isVadEnabled, elevenLabsSettings.turnModel, elevenLabsSettings.isSpeculativeTurnEnabled or elevenLabsSettings.turnEagerness

changes.description: Attributes that differ from the optimized values; set each path to its to value and replace the agent to apply them

effects.description: What applying the changes brings that no attribute holds; backupModels: the agent gains the backup model chain

isAvailable.description: Whether applying the optimized settings would change anything (changes is not empty)

action.description: Action performed when the scenario fires; null means the scenario only replies

actionParameters.description: Action inputs; sendSms takes senderNumber and message

reply.description: What the agent says when the scenario fires

toolId.description: Tool invoked when action is toolCall; must be one of the company's tools

triggerType.description: What activates the scenario; defaults to custom

when.description: Trigger text; required and used only when triggerType is custom

answerQuestions.description: Answer questions from the agent's knowledge

custom.description: Free-form capabilities described by a prompt

extractData.description: Collect structured data during the call

takeMessage.description: Record a message for the company

transferToHuman.description: Hand the call to a human

agentId.description: Target agent id; required together with agentExtension when destination is agent

condition.description: When the call should be transferred

groupId.description: Target group id; required together with groupExtension when destination is group

customProperties.description: Extra context handed to the human agent

includeProperties.description: Context handed to the human agent

isConfirmationRequired.description: Ask the caller to confirm before transferring

createdAt.description: When the knowledge base was created

fileExtension.description: Extension of the stored file: the upload's extension, HTML for a custom source, null for a URL source

name.description: Name of the knowledge base; derived from the filename for an uploaded file

sourceUrl.description: Address the content is read from; null unless sourceType is URL

status.description: Whether the content is ready to be used by a voice agent

updatedAt.description: When the knowledge base was last changed

voiceAgentIds.description: Voice agents the knowledge base is attached to

sourceType.description: Where the content comes from; upload a file through POST /knowledge-bases/files

text.description: Content of the knowledge base; required when sourceType is CUSTOM, rejected otherwise

url.description: Address to read the content from; required when sourceType is URL, rejected otherwise

schemas.description: Only with `include=schema`: the JSON Schema of the full webhook body, keyed by version.

url.description: As stored; the host may come back lowercased and a bare host with a trailing slash.

eventTypes.description: Subscribed event types, sorted. `null` means every event type, including ones added later.

status.description: `disabled`: turned off by you (Dashboard or API). `failing`: turned off automatically after repeated delivery failures; it may be re-enabled automatically, or by you.

secret.description: Only in the create response: the signing secret (`whsec_...`). Absent if it could not be read; then use the secret endpoint.

url.description: `https://` URL on a public host whose name ends in a public top-level domain.

eventTypes.description: Event types to receive (see List webhook event types). Omit or send null for every event type. An empty list is rejected.
Replaces the subscription. `null` subscribes to every event type.

previousSecretExpiresAt.description: When the previous secret stops signing deliveries: 24 hours after the rotation. Until then every delivery carries signatures from both secrets.

id.description: Delivery id; the same value as the `svix-id` header of the delivered request.

eventId.description: The `event_id` of the webhook body, the key to deduplicate on.

status.description: `retrying`: an attempt failed and another is scheduled at `nextAttemptAt`. `failed`: the last attempt failed and no retry is scheduled.

responseStatusCode.description: HTTP status your server answered; 0 when it could not be reached.

responseBody.description: Your server's response body, at most 4 KB. When no HTTP response came back (`responseStatusCode` 0), a fixed message instead.

payload.description: The body that was sent. `null` after the 30-day payload retention.

limit.name: limit
limit.description: Max. number of items in response data.

paginationLimit.name: limit
paginationLimit.description: Maximum number of items to return

paginationOffset.name: offset
paginationOffset.description: Offset the list of returned items by this amount

dialerCampaignContactId.name: campaignContactId
dialerCampaignContactId.description: Campaign-contact (membership) ID — `campaign_contact_id` from the contacts list, not the contact's own id.

dialerExportJobId.name: jobId
dialerExportJobId.description: Export job ID returned by the export enqueue call.

dialerScriptId.name: scriptId
dialerScriptId.description: Script ID (BIGINT serialized as string in responses; send the numeric value).

dialerSurveyId.name: surveyId
dialerSurveyId.description: Survey ID (BIGINT serialized as string in responses; send the numeric value).

basicAuth.description: HTTP Basic Authentication. Use your API Access Key ID as the username and your API Access Key Secret as the password. Generate keys in the CloudTalk Dashboard under Account -> Settings -> API Keys (https://dashboard.cloudtalk.io/menu/account/settings/API-keys).
